posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
So I've been playing a lot of Sentinels lately. So much so I may need a 12 step program soon. But until that days comes, it has become my obsession to figure out a way to get all of Mr. Fixer's styles and weapons out at the same time.

My obsession began after I decided to try and beat every villain in the game with a single team of 4 heros. A super team I like to call "Punch All the Faces". It consists of Legacy, Team Leader Tachyon, Chrono Ranger, and Mr. Fixer. I was battling The Chairman in the Time Cataclysm when this wonderous event which I'd only read about in the forums occurred. Mr. Fixer had his Jackhandle out and Dual Crowbars in hand when the environment played Fixed Point. I finally found the ultimate joy of the completely broken killing machine who is Mr. Fixer.

The problem: How do I keep Fixed Point out for multiple rounds, long enough to get all of Mr. Fixer's stuff out?

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
Using Omnitron-X and Rook City Wraith can speed through the Environment deck. Have Ra with Excavation, allowing for repeated stacking of th Environment deck, thus Fixed can always be ontop of the Deck. The Argent Adept can also repeatedly play Vernal Sonata to keep Excavation continueing to be drawn. Once that has been set up, Omnitron-X would switch to using Bio-Engineering Beam to destroy Fixed Point, allowing it to be in the trash when Ra plays Excavation.

The turn order would be something like: Rook City Wraith, The ARgent Adept, Mister Fixer, Omnitron-X, and Ra. Rook City Wraith being first just in case Fixed Point is revealed, allowing it to be used that round.

On that note, I have a question that probably has been discussed at some point, but I don't remember seeing. I know from this discussion that if Santa Guise causes Limited cards to be revealed that were already in play that they'd go into the trash, but:

  1. Is this the same for when no Limited cards were already in play, but multiple are revealed?
  2. Is this the same if Fixed Point is out, or would this allow multiple Limited cards to be in play?
I'm guessing the answers are 1) the first card would go into play, the duplicates would go to the trash, and 2) the duplicates are going to the trash without ever entering play (and aren't being destroyed along the way), and so Fixed Point doesn't change anything?

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked: We talked to Christopher about this last week. What you describe is what happens in the video game right now, but there's a problem: the card is already in play, it's just face down. The solution we arrived upon is that if a limited card is flipped face up, and there is another copy in play, and Fixed Point is in play, then the limited card just flips back face down and stays where it is.

posts.name: aawood
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

That seems like an odd conclusion based on how Limited cards works and what Santa Guise's power says which is treat them as they just came into play.    Other affects which would try to put a limited or otherwise invalid card into play from top of deck go immediately to the trash.  

My guess is it's the distinction between something entering play, and something being treated as though it had just entered play. In most cases (Limited card exists, another Limited card is being played), they go to the trash instead of entering play, so "coming into play" never happens, and the two cards are never in play at once. In the Santa Guise case (Limited card face-up, another Limited card flips face up), it successfully came into play face-down (meaning the wording on the card wasn't active, included the "limited" keyword), and is already in play when it's flipped face-up; this means we're faced with two Limited cards, both in play, one being treated as though it had just entered play, something that wouldn't normally happen.

Could absolutely be wrong about all this, mind!
